reviews.title: Good but could be great :)
reviews.text:
I really like this app to provide a plan for me to get to my targeted distance.
It was great.
What I don’t like is that now I’m on my second plan it thinks I haven’t done any training. I don’t class myself as an accomplished runner but there doesn’t seem to be any way to have that progress acknowledged.

It’s also frustrating that you can’t schedule in parkrun each Saturday. Getting the sorry we see you didn’t do the full distance today on Saturday’s is not an accurate reflection of what my plan should be. 
I also wondered if there is the possibility of being able to identify your location. Today my plan told me to drink plenty due to the high humidity- it’s 4 degrees in winter. Definitely no humidity here today

I’m going to miss the community part of the app. With it moving to Strava it just doesn’t seem to be the same. The only posts are Runna admin posts - not sure where the community is in that. I sure miss the community, being able to get feedback or encourage others is what I like running for. This app no longer allows that 

I feel like this app is getting worse not better. 
Disappointing

reviews.title: Polished—but basic. 2.5 Stars.
reviews.text:
Runna is a polished app with a great interface, but after repeated technical issues and disappointing training adaptation, I’m giving up on it.

Treadmill runs have been particularly frustrating. The Apple Watch app routinely fails to sync properly with the iPhone app, leaving me without heart rate data. I’ve tried working with support, but the problems persist.

Even more disappointing is the lack of meaningful training adaptation. Despite having access to Apple Health data, Runna doesn’t seem to use recovery metrics or training performance to intelligently adjust workouts.

I’ve been sick for three weeks. During that time, I’ve repeatedly marked myself as ill, cut long runs short, and struggled through interval sessions. Yet the training plan continues unchanged. The AI coach offers plenty of encouragement, but encouragement isn’t coaching. A genuinely adaptive training platform should recognize these patterns and adjust training intensity, volume, and recovery accordingly.  I have communicated this with their team, and while they told me these features are in development (9 months ago), its current state doesn’t justify the cost.

Runna looks great and has plenty of potential, but it feels more like a static training plan wrapped in a beautiful interface than an intelligent running coach.

At this point, I’ll be taking the money I spend on Runna and Strava and investing it in a platform that actually responds to my training and recovery.

reviews.title: Overpriced
reviews.text:
I’ve used this app in the past and it was reasonably priced and really good for guided runs. However, now, the same plans are clearly AI generated, don’t really take into account your wants/needs and they have the audacity to charge £15.99 a month?? I don’t mind an AI generated workout for my needs but there’s no way I’m paying that price for one when alternatives are so much more reasonable. If I were a serious runner with actual distance and pace goals I wouldn’t touch this with a barge pole as it does not help with these goals at all.

The interface is great but again, it’s not worth the price especially for a casual runner. Use C25K (free), intervals pro or another alternative instead.

Also, app on Apple Watch doesn’t even let you skip intervals, I.e you HAVE to do the whole 5min warm up walk… which is really poor.

reviews.title: Fine - until you need advice
reviews.text: I’ve run 9 marathons and ultra marathons and was curious to see how this would work for my 50km ultra. First the good: great syncing with Garmin and Strava, really enjoyed the intervals, yoga, stretch and stability sessions. Now for the not so good. It accepts the ultra race but prepares you for a marathon. And it’s set up for a younger runner. There is just not enough built in recovery for a V50 athlete, the easy paces are too fast, and there’s no option or even advice for xtraining, which is vital for the masters athlete. The strength sessions aren’t sufficient to prepare for an ultra. If something goes awry you get meaningless drivel from an ai chatbot - even when they say you’re taking to a real person. Save your money and join a run club, download a good free training plan from online - talk to other, experienced humans.

reviews.title: The PMs and Engineers should be fired.
reviews.text:
Runna has been a great app thus far, but it’s incredibly buggy, the product team should be ashamed. Here are just a few issues: 1) Runna workouts don’t properly sync exercise minutes to Apple Fitness, unless you start the workout directly from the workout app. Countless threads on reddit about this, but no fix. 2) You can’t add a route to an upcoming run unless you’re on the current week. i’m trying to plan for next week and can’t add routes i’ve created. 3) You can’t view the route map you’ve added, you have to be actively within a work out to see it. I need to be able to navigate to my starting point! 4) The route map doesn’t show up on the apple watch if you start the run from the iphone app. 5) the workout insights are absolutely useless, and you are forced to rate the workout to see them. So much friction in the user experience. 

I’m training for my first half and using Runna due to the Strava brand, but the app is pretty bad. So close to just going old school and following a plan out of a book, since the app creates more friction in my workflow rather than being smooth.

I love the idea of this app - setting custom paces, warm up, cool down stretches.  It gives a great framework to follow, and the plan design seems great.  BUT, there’s a lot of issues. My biggest gripe is that the Apple Watch integration doesn’t work.  I’ve been on 5 runs using this app and only 1 of them has worked the way it’s supposed to (I have the latest Apple Watch).  Most of the time, the app will freeze, pause, not keep track of miles, or sometimes the screen will just be black.  

Feature request: when your run is logged incorrectly (which it normally will be through the watch), there should be a way to edit the runs (or combining data from multiple runs). Would be a great add. 

I’m going to continue using it for the plan design, but won’t be using the Apple Watch features, which is a huge bummer.

I chatted with their customer service chat bot, which wasn’t helpful, they escalated me to a support request with an agent, who got back to me 2 weeks later with a canned response sending me the same upgrade guide link the chat bot had, telling me to wait a year or throw away my Runna premium subscription….

reviews.title: No injuries running… until I started using this app
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like this app, and thought it would be great, so I opted for the year subscription via Strava. Huge mistake. I’ve been running for a few months now injury-free, but since I started using this app, injuries have been creeping in. It just pushes too hard, too fast, and that’s a recipe for injuries. The voice prompts are also the absolute worst. All of the voices they offer sound incredibly robotic and depressing. And while support seems to be responsive (which is good because the releases have been buggy) all of their support messages seem to be written by AI. Whether any are sent by real people or AI agents, I don’t know.

I am currently nursing what appears to be an ACL injury after the latest run. I don’t think I’ll be using the app again. 

If you are new or newish to running, returning to running, whatever, please do not use this app. It’s going to increase volume far too quickly (recent research says no more than 5% per week, and this app seems to double that). It has made me start to hate running, which is terrible. But I’m stuck with the purchase. Just trying to save others.

reviews.title: Paying to be a beta tester?
reviews.text:
I like the concept but the app has some shortcomings I find frustrating. It stands out as being the most frustrating running app I've used if I am honest. That includes both my free and paid experiences. I'll be seeing it through to the end of the training plan at least but I do feel like I am paying to be a beta tester with some of it. I've had to raise many requests to support and they don't always have an answer.

Some things that spring to mind

- Pacing on Apple Watch (Ultra 3) is terrible and close to unusable on shorter intervals for me. Apple Watch activities seem fine themselves
- AI can sometimes re generate things differently if it needs to re run something when you would assume you were always getting an optimised training plan and it shouldn't vary much. A more old school approach could improve this unless it is using an old school approach and it just has bugs
- I have longer run than I should the the day before a race which would typically be less activity
- There is no warm up and cool down built around a race day

reviews.title: Strength Plan Iffy
reviews.text:
Love the running portions of my plan. The strength leaves a LOT to be desired. I’ve checked 5 times that I only have dumbbells selected in my equipment and it keeps including stuff that call for a bench. 

It also seems less than optimal that while you can have the app on your Apple Watch, you cannot track heart rate at all in Runna strength workouts. If you use the Strava watch app or the regular Apple Watch workout app (both of which track HR), there is no way to link them to the Runna activity. If you track the workout in Runna and one of the options that allow for heart rates, you end up with two activities in Strava. Not the biggest deal in the world, but there is definitely a more seamless way to get everything to communicate. My boutique studio gym is able to have their app perfectly synced with Apple activities which in turn sync to Strava— so it’s wild an app (literally centered in technology) can’t get it right. 

Probably wouldn’t have bothered reviewing though if it wasn’t for the equipment issue. That is the thing that was really annoying— having to Google alternative exercises for certain parts of the workout while in the middle of it.

reviews.title: Good in theory but poorly functioning
reviews.text:
I subscribed for Strava+Runna but then it wouldn’t speak to runna so I clicked onto both so I could link the accounts and then they charged me for both. I submitted a ticket and it took them 21 days of silence before they finally tesoonded with too bad sorry. 

That is a prelude to continued disappointment in its function. Often I will run and start the run program through the runna app on my Apple watch and it will give me all the lap prompts which means it’s tracking my pace and distance but then the run will not appear on my runna app or Strava app history for tracking. This happens about 25% of the time. The run will show up on my Apple fitness app though, which makes it odd. 

The inconsistency paired with the poor customer service means I cannot recommend this app. I also don’t think you need the yearly membership which I unfortunately bought and was charged twice for. 

Get it for a month, get a gist of the program, then cancel it and rinse,repeat and adjust for your own abilities. You can do it on your own, I believe in you!

reviews.title: 12 months of not delivering on promised features
reviews.text:
Runna’s been the official digital training partner of parkrun since Jan 1, 2025, but you still can’t adapt your plan around going to one every weekend.

You also can’t arrange for multiple plans, and a new plan has zero information from your previous one.

There’s nothing for ultramarathon runners.

You can’t adapt or adjust individual workouts.

Your plan doesn’t adjust around heart rate or effort.

All of the above features were part of Runna’s roadmap 365 days ago, and still haven’t been delivered, but they’re happy to keep charging 120USD a year.

reviews.title: Sound issues
reviews.text: App was good but now during workouts it reduces the sound of any music app or YouTube to a whisper which makes it almost unusable. If you try to refresh the app to fix it then it changes how far you’ve ran and there isn’t a way to edit this at the end.

reviews.title: Committed Runner, Flawed Algorithm. Honest Feedback After Months of Use
reviews.text:
I used Runna as my primary training tool for several months leading up to a half marathon race day, completing nearly every session with only a few missed workouts due to illness and Ramadan. I was genuinely committed to the program. Unfortunately, the results,  and more importantly, the data, tell a story the app seems unwilling to hear.

The pace predictions were significantly overstated. Even after manually dropping my target by 20–25 seconds per km below the app’s recommendation, I couldn’t sustain it past 6 km on race day. Ended up with a race performance worse than my training. 

More critically: the algorithm ignored clear physiological red flags in the final two weeks. My HRV dropped over 7 points eight days before the race and stayed suppressed until race day. My Garmin flagged my training status as “Strained” during the same period. The taper week did nothing to reverse this. The app had all of this data, and did nothing with it.

The issue isn’t a bad race. It’s that a training platform with months of your biometric and performance data should be able to identify when a runner is being worn down, not built up. The volume, effort zones, paces, and taper logic need serious rethinking.

For casual runners, the structure and guidance may be helpful. But if you train with data and expect the platform to actually use it, you may find it frustrating.

reviews.title: Lack of thought

reviews.title: Good plans, but few bugs
reviews.text: Great plans but I’ve found a small handful of frustrating bugs with the software- main issue is that when using with phone - I opened the camera app and it cut off the run part way through … had to restart … then the run was stuck in the background and unable to get back to where it was left off. GPS was running hours after and have to mess around in the Apple settings to try stop it. Also if you lose signal it’s very latent and doesn’t allow you to start a route so it’s unusable without service…. I will also add their in app AI is poor… for the cost of the the subscription… it’s embarrassing how far behind they are with utilising integrated AI for the individual user triangulation especially how far on this tech has come the past year - if the app was free it would get a strong 4.5. But it’s not so the value to cost is off … hence 2star worthy.

reviews.title: Plan is good, issues with accurate logging. Nonstandard weekly schedule.
reviews.text:
The app continues to log my workouts in the middle of the night even though I am running during the day. This messes with the whole scheduling feature as the app thinks I didn’t do the run on the day I was supposed to and moves that run to the next day. It defeats using the app at all except for getting the initial ai plan. I just have to ignore it telling me when to run. The times are accurate on my watch so it’s not a time zone issue on my phone. I have seen Reddit posts where others are having similar issues and have reached out and been told that it’s not a priority for Runna to address which is….not a great sign that I should spend money on this.

Also, in the US, our weeks start on Sunday. There is no way to modify this in the app either. Other people have reached out about this and Runna has allegedly said this is also not an issue and people just need to adapt. I have many other fitness apps and they have the feature integrated in so I don’t see why Runna also can’t do this. This also messes with scheduling as I have to work in running around two part time jobs that are both based on a work week starting on Sunday.

I can’t recommend others pay for the app if Runna is not willing to address known problems. I myself will not be paying past the initial free plan unless these issues are addressed.

reviews.title: Really disappointed at the price structure
reviews.text: You pay good money for this app but if you don’t pay for annual subscription you can only see four weeks of your plan. I wouldn’t have resubscribed to this app if I knew this. How ridiculous!!

reviews.title: Good training app with very annoying features by design.
reviews.text:
I initially liked Runna as a training platform. However, one design decision completely ruined the experience for me.

Every time you take a screenshot in the app, Runna interrupts you with a popup pushing you to use their “share” feature instead. This happens every single time, and it completely gets in the way if you’re simply trying to capture your workout stats to send to a friend, save for yourself, or reference later.

To be clear:
I do not want to share my workout via the app’s social feature.
I just want to take a normal screenshot like I can in literally every other app.

Instead, the app hijacks the screenshot action and throws a sharing screen in your face. You then have to dismiss it every single time before you can take another screenshot.

This isn’t a bug — support confirmed it’s intentional.

Designing software to interfere with a standard phone function in order to push a sharing feature is incredibly frustrating UX. It feels manipulative rather than helpful.

I raised the issue with support, but the response was essentially “we can’t change it.”

Because of that, I cancelled my subscription.

If Runna ever allows users to disable this behaviour, I’d happily reconsider — but until then this feature alone makes the app far more irritating to use than it should be.

reviews.title: Training jumps up too fast
reviews.text: A shame to be writing this - the functionality of this app is 10/10, the structure, usability and way it’s connects to your watch, Strava etc is fab. However, I used this for a half marathon training block back at the start of 2024 and the training jumped up so fast (2km a week when the furthest I’d ever ran was 7km) the training was too intense and there was no recommendation of supplementary strengthening/stretching to help condition alongside running. As a complete beginner I just followed the plan which led to a really bad injury (stress fracture) which I’m still dealing with almost 2 years later. It would be great if the training would be more tailored and slower progression, or feedback along the way to see how you’re going/feeling. I hate leaving negative reviews but I’d hate for anyone else to be in this position and I believe this app can do amazing things if the actual running programs are tweaked!

reviews.title: BAD!!! AND ESPECIALLY IF YOU HAVE A POLAR WATCH
reviews.text:
For credibility 
HM: 1:22
10k: 38:02
5k: 18:45

This app has no integration with Polar. They keep saying it’s in the pipe.. meanwhile, they roll out useless features. AI summaries are hilariously bad. Like I read them as a joke.

From a training standpoint, way too much intensity. Tempo, intervals and long run with tempo blocks all in the same week is not a good idea, even if you’re a performance athlete. 

I like the calendar integration and (some of) the variety in runs, but that’s it. And some runs are just plain idiotic. Why, for example, have a 2 week focus on 200m intervals for a marathon program? 

There’s just too much wrong with this app to say I’d recommend. In fact, I actively discourage.
